name: Exxon Mobil

header.one_liner: Peak refining margins from Middle East disruption doubled earnings; we value Exxon on what lasts.
header.thesis: Exxon earned $15.4B in the third quarter, double a year earlier, as supply restrictions through the Strait of Hormuz pushed refining margins to historic highs: Energy Products alone earned $7.2B against $1.8B. Upstream grew too, despite 273,000 fewer barrels a day from Middle East and Kazakhstan disruptions. The question is how much of this lasts once supply returns.

base.eps_label: FY2026E EPS excluding identified items: nine months about $8.90 (earnings $34.1B plus $2.7B of identified-item losses) plus a fourth quarter near the third-quarter run rate
base.rev_label: FY2026E total revenues ($B), near consensus, with Q3 at $113.2B

rev_cagr.why: Revenue rose about a third on higher prices and refining margins caused by Middle East supply disruption. The base case assumes prices and margins drift back toward their 10-year range as supply returns, offset partly by Permian, Guyana and LNG growth.

margin_end.why: Net margin is about 12% this year with refining margins above their 10-year range. The base case brings it back toward 10%, still above the 2024 to 2025 level because of cost savings and advantaged barrels.

share_chg.why: Exxon repurchased $15.1B of stock in nine months, about 2.5% of its market value a year.

exit_pe.why: In the more normal years 2023 to 2025 Exxon traded at 12.2x, 14.5x and 16.6x that year’s EPS (average price over the year); at the 2022 peak it traded at 6.9x. The base case applies the 14.5x median to mid-cycle EPS, the bear case the low end, the bull case the high end.
exit_pe.source: Moat Monitor price history and reported EPS, 2022 to 2025

pillars.title: Refining is the windfall
pillars.claim: Energy Products earned $7.2B in the quarter vs $1.8B a year earlier, as global refining margins rose above their 10-year range.

evidence.t: Global refining margins increased to historically high levels with unavailable capacity

pillars.test: Do refining margins fall back as Middle East capacity returns?

pillars.title: Upstream grows despite disruption
pillars.claim: Upstream earned $7.1B vs $5.7B; price added $3.7B while Middle East volumes cost $0.9B.

evidence.t: Production 4.5M oil-equivalent barrels a day, down 273k on Middle East and Kazakhstan disruptions and Guyana entitlements

pillars.test: Do Permian and Guyana growth offset the disruption?

pillars.title: Chemicals are weak
pillars.claim: Chemical margins fell further below the bottom of their 10-year range, though earnings rose to $0.7B from a weak base.

pillars.title: Capital discipline
pillars.claim: Cash capex fell to $7.0B in the quarter while $28B was returned to shareholders in nine months.

evidence.t: Dividends $12.9B and buybacks $15.1B in nine months; capex $20.0B

pillars.test: Is the $20B a year buyback pace sustained when prices fall?

variant.street: The market pays about 14x this year's earnings, the top of the integrated oils, for Exxon's growth and discipline.
variant.ours: This year's earnings include a refining windfall from disrupted Middle East supply. Our base case lets prices and margins normalise, which leaves the shares above our 12-month target.
variant.could_be_wrong: If disruption persists through 2027 and Permian and Guyana growth adds volume, earnings stay high and the multiple holds.
variant.would_change_mind: Refining margins staying above their 10-year range into 2027, or the price falling toward 11x normalised earnings.

review.basis: Q3 2026 10-Q (quarter to 30 September 2026). Q4 reports in late January; this review refreshes after the print.
review.headline: Earnings doubled on a refining windfall from disrupted Middle East supply. The business is strong; this year's profit is not the run rate.
review.model: Exxon finds and produces oil and gas (Upstream), refines it into fuels (Energy Products), and makes chemicals and lubricants (Chemical and Specialty Products). Profit depends mostly on oil and gas prices and refining margins.

how_it_earns.v: Oil and gas production: Permian, Guyana, LNG. The largest earner over a cycle.
Refining and fuels marketing. Earns the gap between crude and fuel prices.
Plastics and petrochemicals. Margins are near decade lows.
Lubricants and specialty chemicals. Steadier margins.

base.story: Middle East supply returns over 2027; refining margins fall back; Permian and Guyana growth and buybacks cushion EPS.

downside.story: Supply returns quickly while demand slows; oil and refining margins fall below the 10-year average.
downside.needs: A global slowdown with restored supply

upside.story: Disruption persists and volume growth resumes; earnings stay near this year's level.

risks.how: Over 40% of this quarter's segment earnings came from refining margins lifted by unavailable capacity.
Upstream earnings move with crude and gas realisations; price added $3.7B to Q3 upstream earnings.
Disruption cut volumes and caused impairments; escalation could cut more.
Chemical margins are below their 10-year range on new capacity in Asia.
Climate policy and lower long-run oil demand could reduce the value of long-lived assets.

peer_read.why_premium: Exxon has the lowest-cost growth barrels among the majors in the Permian and Guyana, and the strongest balance sheet.
peer_read.why_not: Shell and TotalEnergies trade at about 8x to 9x next-year earnings with similar exposure to the same windfall.
peer_read.peers_note: European majors trade at lower multiples partly for policy and listing reasons.

questions: What are normalised earnings once Middle East supply returns?
Is a premium to European majors justified?
Will buybacks hold at $20B a year if prices fall?

arguments.label: Growth
arguments.text: Earnings rose to $15.4B from $7.5B, mainly on price and refining margins. Production fell 273,000 barrels a day on Middle East and Kazakhstan disruptions despite Permian and Guyana growth.

arguments.label: Moat
arguments.text: Low-cost Permian and Guyana barrels, integrated refining and chemicals, and scale. Prices, set by geopolitics, still decide most of the earnings.

arguments.label: Profitability

thesis_long: Exxon is having an exceptional year. Restricted supply through the Strait of Hormuz and lost refining capacity pushed refining margins to historic highs and international gas prices above their 10-year range. Third-quarter earnings doubled to $15.4B; Energy Products alone earned $7.2B, nearly four times a year earlier. Underneath, the company is executing well: Permian and Guyana are growing, costs are falling and capex is down.

The question is what to pay for a windfall. Production actually fell 273,000 barrels a day on Middle East and Kazakhstan disruptions, and the extra profit came from prices and margins that depend on supply staying short. Consensus already expects 2027 EPS to fall about 12%. At about 14x this year's earnings, Exxon trades at the top of the majors.

Our base case lets prices and refining margins normalise over three years, partly offset by volume growth and $20B a year of buybacks. On that path the 12-month target is below today's price. We would turn positive if refining margins stayed above their 10-year range into 2027, or if the price fell toward 11x normalised earnings.

upside_risks.how: If Middle East supply stays restricted through 2027, refining and gas earnings stay near this year's level.
Restored Middle East volumes on top of Permian and Guyana growth would lift upstream earnings even at lower prices.

dcf.label: Mid-cycle EPS, because this year’s windfall is not a base to grow from

valuation.hist_label: Reported diluted EPS, 2022 to 2025 (SEC filings). 2022 includes the Russia impairment; forecasts exclude identified items
valuation.why: Oil earnings swing with prices and refining margins. Mid-cycle EPS averages 2022 to 2025 reported results with this year’s windfall and our three-year path as margins normalise, so the target does not capitalise one unusual year.

variant_view.label: EPS the price capitalises
variant_view.why: At $180 and Exxon’s normal 14.5x the market is capitalising about $12.40 of EPS, close to this year’s windfall. Our mid-cycle EPS across 2022 to 2029 is about $10.30.

proof.event: Q4 2026 results: refining margins and realised prices as Middle East supply normalises
